items.problem: Skill instructs the agent to compile with `winapp build`, which is not a real CLI command.
items.evidence: build session-log turn 63: `winapp build` → "'build' was not matched. Unrecognized command or argument 'build'." exit 1; agent recovered with `dotnet build` in turn 64.
items.wrong_text_if_any: SKILL.md: 'winapp build  # compile; never run the .exe directly' (Step 3); 'Prefer `winapp build` to compile' (build-discipline note); 'After PASS, do a final `winapp build`' (Step 4); Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 header 'winapp build then this script'; MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md 'The benchmark's `winapp build` injects...'
items.root_cause: The plugin moved to native `dotnet build`/`dotnet run` but several instruction sites still name the removed `winapp build` wrapper.
items.proposed_fix: Replace every `winapp build` reference with `dotnet build` (run sync with an exit sentinel), and add a one-line note that no `winapp build` subcommand exists.
items.generalizes: Every migration ends with a compile/confirm step; an instruction to run a non-existent command wastes a turn on each scenario regardless of the app.

items.problem: Copied UWP `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs` causes CS0579 duplicate-attribute build failures; skill has no guidance for it.
items.evidence: session-log turns 56-59: 6x `error CS0579: Duplicate 'System.Reflection.Assembly*Attribute'` at obj\...\BackgroundTask.AssemblyInfo.cs; fixed by blanking Tasks/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs (build 6 errors → 0).
items.root_cause: Old-style UWP/.NET-Framework projects ship assembly attributes in Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs; SDK-style WinUI 3 projects set GenerateAssemblyInfo=true and emit the same attributes, so they collide when the file is copied.
items.proposed_fix: Add a MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md section: on CS0579 duplicate AssemblyAttribute errors, delete the copied Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs (with a Get-ChildItem snippet); do not set GenerateAssemblyInfo=false.
items.generalizes: Essentially every UWP project carries Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs, so this collision recurs whenever such files (including sub-project ones) are copied into the SDK-style tree.

items.problem: UWP `windows.backgroundTasks` (and `windows.appService`) <Extension> manifest entries with in-process EntryPoints break AppX deployment (0x80080204); skill's manifest checklist doesn't cover them.
items.evidence: session-log turn 60: winapp run 'App manifest validation error ... EntryPoint="Tasks.SampleBackgroundTask" without ActivatableClassId in windows.activatableClass.inProcessServer (0x80080204)'; fixed turn 61 by removing the <Extensions> blocks.
items.skill_search: grep 'backgroundTasks|ActivatableClass|appService|0x80080204' across winui-uwp-migration → no hits; manifest checklist (Windows.Desktop + runFullTrust) stops at item 4 (EntryPoint placeholder).
items.root_cause: A packaged WinUI 3 desktop app does not auto-generate the windows.activatableClass.inProcessServer/ActivatableClass registration UWP's toolchain produced, so an in-process background-task EntryPoint resolves to nothing and AppX validation rejects the manifest.
items.proposed_fix: Add item 5 to the manifest checklist: drop in-process windows.backgroundTasks/windows.appService <Extension> blocks for structural migrations (the C# task class still compiles), or author the full activatable-class registration and otherwise defer.
items.generalizes: In-process background tasks and app services are a common UWP manifest pattern across many SDK samples; any such app hits the same 0x80080204 deploy failure when its manifest is carried over verbatim.
